penetration_assumption: TWO methods, converging. (1) Bottom-up, the number I actually rely on: nine pad SKUs that PROVED demand at ARY's own till and then went dark on zero stock. Each is annualised at its OWN observed in-stock run-rate (sales while stocked / months it was stocked x 12): Sofy Super Value 290mm Rs 5,400/mo, Sofy Anti-Bacteria 28s Rs 4,085/mo, Sofy Body Fit Pro 290mm Rs 3,145/mo, Secure 280mm Rs 2,046/mo, Whisper Ultra Nights XL+ Rs 1,900/mo, Bindazzz Nights Rs 1,746/mo, Whisper Choice 6 Regular Rs 1,480/mo, Sanjhee 18N Rs 1,475/mo, Stayfree XL 12N Rs 872/mo = Rs 2,65,788 gross, less the Rs 71,788 they already earned = Rs 1,94,000 incremental. Then TWO haircuts I apply deliberately: x0.60 for cannibalisation (a woman buying the Rs 450 value pack is not purely incremental - she would otherwise have bought ~7 of the Rs 45 packs), and x0.89 for the vacation window (VERIFIED seasonality: 27 days from ~26 Dec the town trades at 35% of normal). = Rs 1,03,600. I round the availability line to Rs 1,20,000 to allow for the two thinnest run-rates. (2) Top-down cross-check: 7,370 packs x ~6.5 pads = ~47,900 pads/yr across an ESTIMATED ~1,700 menstruating women = 28 pads/woman/year, about 2.3 per cycle against a 10-15 per cycle need - so ARY captures roughly 20% of on-campus demand. Lifting that to ~27% yields +Rs 1.5 L. Two independent methods landing at Rs 1.0-1.5 L is why I state Rs 1.2 L rather than a single-method number. The remaining Rs 22,000 is new lines: 2 extra panty-liner facings (~Rs 10,000; the current single Carefree SKU does Rs 2,277 on 5 units of stock) and one maternity-pad line (~Rs 12,000, sized off the babycare lane's ~32 births/yr, not off a market share). The ~1,700 denominator is the weakest input and is NOT verified - the vault's own Population.md calls the cohort split "the weakest number in the whole" study; it is my build-up from VERIFIED enrolments (Eternal University 1,102, Akal Academy ~1,250, School of Spiritual Sciences 305, AIRWE 487 rural women, ~700-1,300 staff family members) with an assumed female share and menstruating-age share. Range 1,400-2,100. Note the top-down method is only a cross-check: I do NOT bank the full 80% shortfall, because residents go home, some use cloth, and no campus store captures 100%.
probe_evidence: The diff's femcare verdicts are almost entirely name-match artefacts and I discarded them. It "covered" the PCOS line by matching the string 250, menopause by matching 875, menstrual cup wash by matching wash (395 SKUs), tampons by matching sofy, and menstrual cups by matching safe. Re-probed every line individually. GENUINELY ABSENT, zero SKUs across all 21,479: tampon=0, menstrual=0, silicone cup=0, prega/pregnancy/preg/hcg/velocit/ovulation=0, meftal/cyclopam/combiflam/paracetamol=0, folic/autrin/dexorange/fefol=0, maternity=0, breast/lactation=0, clotrimazole/canesten=0, heat patch=0, feminine=0, vaginal/private/ph balance/lactic=0, niine=0. Terms that returned rows but are ARTEFACTS, each inspected row-by-row: ican=58 SKUs (matches "American"/"Mexican"); nursing=11 (student uniforms and cardigans - this is a nursing college); cranberry=8 (Real juice, Bournville, W2 body wash); candid=3 (Candid PRICKLY HEAT POWDER, not clotrimazole); liner=5 (Faber Castell text liner, Blue Heaven EYE liner); disposal=25 (disposable GLASSES); iron=33 (Bajaj/Havells electric irons, iron kadai, iron tawa); hygiene=1 (Surf Excel Active Hygiene); bella=30 (Bellavita perfume); rio=15 (Orion Chocopie); uti=25 (substring). THE CATCH THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER: my intimate/vwash/everteen/sirona/pee safe/carmesi/azah probes all returned 0 and I was about to call intimate wash a genuine gap. Probing "v wash" with a space found V Wash 100Ml - 38 units, Rs 7,720, LAST SALE 2026-08-30, 42 units in stock, purchased 2026-07-31, and filed under subgroup "Cream", not any hygiene subgroup. Intimate wash is stocked, selling and live. That is the fifth instance of this exact failure mode in this exercise and it is why I did not report a larger gap. Also confirmed the 6 hits on pregn/prega/ovul/i-can/tampon/menstr are all false: Nayasa Cane Mug, Skoodle Canister, Aarti Candle, Diwali Candles, Pepsi Can 250/300 - matching "can". Sanjhee/Seabird/Pro Ease/Unicare/Supercare/Anion are all real but dormant ARY pad brands.

DELIST, do not stock - 62 dormant pad SKUs, 37 of which have NEVER been purchased once in the system's lifetime. They are duplicate re-keyings of the same 4-5 products: 'Whisper Choice 7 Pads' / 'Whisper Choice 7 Pad' / 'Whisper Whisper Choice 7' / 'Whisper Whisper Choice 8 Pads' / 'Whisper Choice Xl 6 Pads' / 'Whisper Choice Xl+ 44 Pads', plus one SKU literally named 'Personal Care'. Buying against this list is the single most expensive mistake available here.
blockers: NOT a sourcing blocker - and this is what makes the verdict availability, not assortment. VERIFIED: three distributors already invoice pads to Baru Sahib - Himachal Wholesale Syndicate (20 bills, Rs 2,30,900, last 2026-07-31), Nirman Associates Pvt Ltd (8 bills, Rs 1,20,515, last 2026-08-11), Baghat Enterprises (6 bills, Rs 47,235, last 2026-08-13). Pads were bought 2.5 weeks ago and the night pads still were not reordered. The constraint is buyer reorder discipline - there is no min/max on these codes - not supplier reach from Rajgarh.

DRUG LICENCE - hard legal blocker on the highest-essentiality absent line. Period-pain OTC (Meftal Spas, Cyclopam, Combiflam) needs a Form 20/21 retail drug licence ARY does not hold. The licence-map and pharmacy lanes found ARY is ALREADY selling allopathic drugs without it (Rs 41,023 / 613 bills), a live exposure carrying a minimum Rs 1 lakh fine and 3-5 years. Adding cramp tablets would deepen an existing breach. Iron+folic sits in the same grey zone. Excluded from the number - do not size these until the licence exists.

CULTURAL / DEMOGRAPHIC, not shelf - the reason I did NOT size tampons or menstrual cups despite both being verified absent. Baru Sahib is a conservative Sikh residential campus of largely unmarried students. Internal-use products have near-zero penetration in rural India (tampon use is well under 1% nationally). A menstrual cup is additionally value-DESTROYING here: a one-time Rs 300-500 purchase that then removes a recurring Rs 45-95/month pad customer. Recommending cups would reduce category revenue, not grow it.

PRIVACY AT THE TILL - pregnancy and ovulation kits are verified absent but are the wrong product for this store. On a closed campus where the cashier knows every buyer, and with a Trust hospital on site running 43,706-47,848 free OPD visits a year, this demand will not surface at an ARY counter. Sized at zero deliberately.

CAPITAL - trivial and not a constraint. Restocking all nine dark SKUs at their ledger cost is roughly Rs 25,000-30,000 of working capital at normal cover. This is a rounding error against a Rs 7.67 Cr business; the reason it has not happened is attention, not money.

SHELF AND PLACEMENT - a real operational finding, not a barrier. VERIFIED: 1,021 packs / Rs 76,749 (17.5% of pad sales) go through the 'Ary Clothing' counter, not the main POS. Whoever fixes reordering must set min/max at BOTH counters or the fix only reaches 82% of the demand.

CONFIDENCE LIMIT - stated plainly. Sales, stock, cost, margin and supplier facts are VERIFIED from live queries. The ~1,700 menstruating-women denominator is ESTIMATED and is the weakest input; the vault's own Population.md calls the cohort split its weakest number. Two of the nine run-rates (Sofy Super Value, Sofy Body Fit Pro) rest on only 2 months of history each and carry the most error - together they are Rs 1,02,540 of the Rs 2,65,788 gross, which is why the 0.60 haircut is applied before I quote anything.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but the headline gap claim does not survive and the reason matters. The coverage diff reported 46.9% coverage with 40.6% "commodity-only", implying a broad specialty gap across intimate wash, menstrual cups, tampons, liners and supplements. Almost all of that is name-match noise - it scored the PCOS line "covered" by matching the digits 250 in a product name and menopause by matching 875. Re-probing each line individually collapses the picture to two facts. FIRST: the one specialty line that looked like a genuine, sizeable gap - intimate wash - is stocked and selling. V Wash 100Ml, 38 units, Rs 7,720, last sale 2026-08-30, 42 in stock, purchased 2026-07-31, filed under subgroup "Cream". My own intimate/vwash/everteen/sirona/pee-safe/carmesi/azah probes ALL returned zero and I was one step from reporting a false gap; only probing "v wash" with a space found it. SECOND: what is genuinely absent is either legally blocked (period-pain OTC, iron+folic - no drug licence, and ARY is already in breach), culturally dead (tampons, menstrual cups on a conservative campus of unmarried students), structurally served elsewhere (pregnancy tests, against a free campus hospital OPD), or negligible (maternity pads at ~32 births/yr). Total genuinely-absent value: about Rs 22,000/yr, of which only ~Rs 10,000 is a true new line. Meanwhile the category is a textbook instance of the exercise's central finding: 83 pad SKUs listed against 21 selling (3.95x over-listing, WORSE than the store-wide 3.14x), 62 dormant, 37 never purchased once in the system's lifetime, and every single night pad, every large/value pack and both 290mm SKUs sitting at zero stock for 1-7 months while the three distributors that supply them invoiced ARY 2.5 weeks ago. Femcare is Rs 4,47,487 - 0.583% of a Rs 7.67 Cr business, Rs 95 per resident per year - against an estimated ~20% capture of on-campus pad demand. The money is entirely in reordering nine codes ARY already owns, and the correct SKU-lines-to-add count is 3, not the 30+ the research corpus implies. Buying against the dormant list would be the actively harmful move.
